extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, trademark practitioners, patent agents/attorneys, applicants, and counsel appearing before the PTAB or TTAB (including newer practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: An overview of procedures, standards, and practice requirements for proceedings before the USPTO administrative tribunals: the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) and the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB). Covers jurisdictional limits, filing/timing requirements, evidentiary rules, standards of review, hearing logistics, and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB jurisdiction limited to questions of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction is limited to questions of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrative tribunal reviews agency decisions and decides whether claims in issued patents are patentable when challenged by third parties; it follows binding law and agency policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB judge qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB judges must possess a law degree and a technical degree; must be a member in good standing of a state/DC/territory bar; must have significant, specialized experience in the patent field and education and/or work experience in science or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are patent attorneys, law clerks, paralegals, administrators, and support staff assist judges. The Board composition, duties, and qualifications are statutorily mandated (35 U.S.C. §6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition and decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB decisions are normally made by panels (usually three judges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute mandates panel form of decision-making for appeals, derivation proceedings, post-grant and inter partes reviews. Panels may produce majority opinions, concurrences, and dissents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of PTAB proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB handles appeals in ex parte patent applications, reexamination proceedings (ex parte and inter partes), reissues, interferences/derivations, inter partes reviews (IPR), and post-grant reviews (PGR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand which proceeding fits the dispute because procedural rules and grounds differ between types (e.g., IPR vs PGR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeals process and required steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal process includes Notice of Appeal & Fee, Appeal Brief, Examiner’s Answer, Appeal Brief Forwarding Fee, Decision by Board; Reply Brief and Request for Oral Hearing (with fee) are optional; Rehearing request and further appeal follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flowchart overview: request for continued examination, office actions, applicant responses, final office action, appeal brief, Examiner’s answer, review by PTAB. No new evidence is permitted during ex parte appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new evidence or argument at PTAB hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence and argument must already be in the record; new evidence is not permitted and new argument is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB hearings differ from district court trials. The hearing is an opportunity to persuade the panel that the existing record supports your position and to answer judges’ questions about the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and conduct of PTAB hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing is an opportunity to persuade the panel the record supports your position and to answer the judges’ questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges enter hearings having reviewed the record and with questions they want answered; focus responses on the record rather than courtroom theatrics. Refer to specific demonstratives, papers, or exhibits by slide and page number. Hearings may be in-person or remote; hearing transcript becomes part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge pre-hearing preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the hearing, judges review the record and hold an internal pre-hearing conference to crystallize key issues and walk through evidence of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges usually will have questions and facts to be confirmed; they make no decision before the hearing but are prepared to probe dispositive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grounds in petition (AIA trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: Only on §102 and §103 grounds, and only on the basis of prior art consisting of patents and printed publications. PGR: On any grounds for invalidity (except best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct proceeding type because permitted grounds differ; best mode is not a ground in PGR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for initiating review (institution thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: 'A reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail' with respect to at least one challenged claim. PGR: 'More likely than not that at least one claim is unpatentable' or the petition raises 'a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the gateway standards the Board applies to decide whether to institute an AIA trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof in AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard of proof is a 'preponderance of the evidence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preponderance is lower than the 'clear and convincing evidence' standard required to prevail in district courts; affects evidence strategy and burden of persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Final Written Decision in AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Final written decision issued within 12 months of institution; can extend by 6 months, but only for 'good cause.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, the entire process (petition to termination or final decision) will take 18 months or less; schedule expectations and planning should reflect these timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible outcomes in AIA proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes include: Deny institution; Settle; Dismiss; Request for Adverse Judgment; Final Written Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final written decisions' dispositions can find all challenged claims unpatentable, mixed outcomes (some unpatentable, some patentable), or find all challenged claims patentable. Joined cases may be excluded from some statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB judge focus: record-centric decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: APJs are concerned with the record, not with how well you work a courtroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APJs have legal and scientific training and come to hearings with knowledge of technology, background, prior art, and the evidence and arguments of record; present arguments tightly linked to record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB docket and case processing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: When a case is appealed, it is docketed, jurisdiction transfers from examiner, a panel is assigned, judges confer, oral hearing (if requested), post-hearing conference, circulate opinion, issue decision, rehearing request, and appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow administrative SOPs (e.g., SOP1 for panel assignment) and be mindful of each processing stage and associated deadlines/fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB judge count and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Board composition includes Chief Judge, Deputy Chief Judge, Vice Chief Judges, Senior Lead Judges, Lead Judges, and Judges; support staff assist judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding roles helps practitioners know who issues orders, who drafts decisions, and where to seek information or guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeals: no new evidence; briefs and hearing optional
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte appeals, no new evidence is permitted during appeal; appellant and examining attorney submit briefs and appellant may request an oral hearing (participation in person or by video).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing limits for filing appeals apply; refer to flowchart/process overview for steps between final office action and PTAB review.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB limited jurisdiction and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: TTAB considers only the right to registration, not the right to use; TTAB may not resolve related issues like contract or licensing disputes; TTAB cannot award damages or attorney fees, or issue injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although remedies are limited, TTAB proceedings can be faster and less expensive than court litigation; choose forum accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB ex parte appeal timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Must file an appeal within a set period from issuance of final office action: three months for an application (optional three-month extension for fee); six months for a Madrid application; three months for a registration (optional one-month extension for fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new evidence permitted during appeal; both appellant and examining attorney submit briefs; appellant may request an oral hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark grounds for refusal (§2 and related sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds include Trademark Act Section 2: §2(a) deceptive (no longer immoral or scandalous; no longer disparaging), §2(b) official insignia, §2(c) name or likeness of living individual, §2(d) likely to cause confusion, §2(e)(1)-(5) (merely descriptive, geographic descriptiveness, surname, functional matter, etc.). Also §3 (service marks), §4 (collective/certification marks), §5 (use by related companies), §6 (disclaimers), §23 (Supplemental Register).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the statutory bases for refusals and how recent Supreme Court decisions affect interpretations (e.g., Iancu v. Brunetti; Matal v. Tam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition filing timing and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration may be opposed by any party believing it would be damaged by registration; opposer must file a notice of opposition within thirty days of publication or within a granted extension; must include the filing fee; may be based on any ground for refusal of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial opposition period is 30 days from Official Gazette publication; extensions of time to oppose may be granted up to a maximum of 180 days; fees apply for certain extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation timing and available grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation (after registration) is similar to opposition but filed after registration: within five years of registration cancellation may be based on any ground for refusal; after three years of registration — expungement; after five years — grounds for cancellation are limited and grounds like likelihood of confusion and descriptiveness are not available after five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing since registration affects which grounds remain available; plan challenges accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings standard in TTAB inter partes proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings define the issues: Complaint (notice of opposition or petition for cancellation) must consist of a 'short and plain' statement of entitlement (reasons plaintiff believes it will be damaged) and grounds (provide fair notice and be plausible). Answer responds and may assert affirmative defenses; counterclaim to cancel pleaded registrations is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleadings must provide fair notice and plausibility; failing to state a claim may lead to motion to dismiss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery framework in TTAB inter partes proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery includes a discovery conference (topics: discovery planning, Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)), initial disclosures under Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a), interrogatory requests, requests for production, depositions, requests for admission, and expert disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board participates in the discovery conference; identify individuals likely to have discoverable information and documents supporting claims/defenses; discovery is subject to TTAB rules and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial evidence periods and rules in TTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-trial disclosures and trial testimony periods: Plaintiff’s trial period – 30 days (testimony by deposition or affidavit; notices of reliance for documentary evidence including discovery materials, registrations, printed publications); Defendant’s trial period – 30 days; Rebuttal period – 15 days (must respond to defendant’s evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rules (e.g., Rule 2.120(j)(3)(i), Rule 2.122(d)(2), Rule 2.122(e)) for what may be relied upon; ensure notices of reliance and testimony are timely and comply with format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing rules and page limits in TTAB trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs are written arguments on law and facts; no new evidence; attachments discouraged and usually ignored; page limits strictly enforced. Cite to evidence by referencing the TTABVUE record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits: Plaintiff’s brief — 55 pages maximum (due 60 days after close of rebuttal testimony); Defendant’s brief — 55 pages maximum (due 30 days after plaintiff’s brief due date); Rebuttal brief — 25 pages maximum (due 15 days after defendant’s brief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing rules in TTAB inter partes proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral hearings are scheduled only at the request of either party; attendance of non-requesting party is not required; participation may be in person or by video; hearings are not a formal part of the record and there is no transcript or recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new evidence or testimony is permitted at the oral hearing; hearing is primarily an opportunity to argue based on the existing record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision composition and content (TTAB and PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions are explanations of the Board’s judgment issued by a panel of three administrative judges and require consideration of all relevant evidence and arguments; include findings of fact and conclusions of law. Dissenting and concurring opinions are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A judge who disagrees may write a dissent; a judge who agrees with result but not reasoning may write a concurrence. Decisions may be appealed to the CAFC or reviewed in district court in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated proceedings and dispositive motion standards (TTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim when facts alleged do not constitute grounds for relief. Motion for summary judgment when no genuine dispute of material fact exists and movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. Accelerated Case Resolution (ACR) is similar to summary judgment but the Board may determine disputed facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these vehicles to resolve cases efficiently when appropriate factual disputes are absent or limited; ACR may produce quicker finality but involves tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative dispute resolution and suspension for settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may negotiate, arbitrate, or mediate; TTAB will suspend proceedings to allow settlement negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension/suspension to permit settlement is commonly granted; consider ADR early to reduce costs and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review options and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review must be taken within sixty-three days of final decision. Appeals to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit are on the administrative record. United States District Court review is de novo and allows new testimony or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose forum carefully: CAFC reviews the administrative record; district court may allow new evidence and a de novo trial; timing and procedural differences affect post-decision strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB publications, rules, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Key resources include Trademark Statute and Rules, Trademark Act (15 USC §1051 et seq.), Rules of Practice in Trademark Cases (37 CFR §2.1 et seq.), Representation rules (37 CFR Parts 10 & 11), TTAB Manual of Procedure (TBMP), TMEP, TTABVUE, TTAB decision summaries, and the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources for detailed procedural guidance, precedential decisions, and filing access; TTABVUE is the electronic docket and case file system for citing record evidence.
